I think this is a mistake in the referenced patch.  Leaving as is.

Hey Brad — recently there’s been some work toward establishing a standard clang-tidy configuration for OpenBMC. The proposed configuration is available here:  https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/style/cpp/.clang-tidy. Would you mind adding the new checks in docs ? 

When we tried to add new checks, It was suggested that we first document any new checks within the style guide and then gradually apply those checks across the repositories. This approach helps ensure consistent settings across all repositories and improves predictability, particularly when issues arise due to clang version upgrades.

Thanks Manoj for the review.

> Would you mind adding the new checks in docs ?

There is already a review in flight: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/82776

> When we tried to add 

You tried?  I'm confused.  Aren't you the maintainer of this code?  Is there some higher authority you answer to?

> This approach helps ensure consistent settings across all repositories

Consistency is a great thing to strive for.  But I don't believe it should be an impediment to improving code quality right now.

I worry that unified consensus will take years or never occur (just look at the age of the review I linked above).  Does that mean we should all stop working on adhering to the cpp core guidelines?

> You tried? I'm confused. Aren't you the maintainer of this code? Is there some higher authority you answer to?

You know the answer to this question because it has already been discussed with you on Discord previously with respect to other repositories.

Yes, every single maintainer, myself included, answers to the "higher authority" of the consensus of the project.  There are directions I also don't like, but we have to work with others.

Expectations of a subproject owner (aka maintainer) are identified here:
https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/community-membership.md#subproject-owner

A relevant one for this discussion is (emphasis mine for clarity):
> Keep abreast of technical changes to the overall project and maintain and/or delegate maintenance of the subproject to _keep it aligned with the overall project_.

---
> There is already a review in flight: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/82776

I'd also like this stack put in in close proximity because it adds a lot of clarifications on why we've chosen specific checks and not others.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/82894

Neither Ed or I have particularly prioritized this work in the last few months.  Since it seems like there is some renewed interest in this, I'll try to get the feedback addressed for mine and Ed's commit sequences in the next few days.

> There are directions I also don't like, but we have to work with others.

Ok sure, I am probably unfairly putting Manoj in a tight spot.  Sorry Manoj.

Maybe my perspective helps you understand my frustration.  At the end of the day, I'm trying to improve the pldm code by complying with the cpp core guidelines, which are already a stated objective of OpenBMC.  To prevent mistakes going forward, I'm leveraging tooling we already have in place to prevent them.  What possible value could there be in impeding/delaying that?

I'm afraid the answer is consistency and my take there is that consistency is something you forever strive towards, not something that is accomplished and thus, should never get in the way of forward progress.

> What possible value could there be in impeding/delaying that?

The reason for putting the breaks on clang-tidy stuff is that it can impede our ability to move to a new clang version.  We had many cases in the past where people put in random clang-tidy checks, which have been found to be fragile, and weren't around to help untangle the issues when it was time to upgrade the compiler.  As a project we made a conscious decision that we want to vet clang-tidy adds, rather than them being a one-off in individual sub-projects.  We are making the trade-off of overall project velocity against potential local bug-catches.

In this case the consistency isn't "we want all the code to look the same", which you are right, it is never accomplished.  The consistency we're aiming for in this case is "we want all the sub-projects to behave the same so we can reason about how we're going to be able to manage them at a organization level".  This consistency, I think, is achievable.

> where people put in random clang-tidy checks

But this isn't random clang-tidy checks.  It's cppcoreguidelines-special-member-functions.  So I have to ask again, what possible value could there be in impeding fixing instances of cppcoreguidelines-special-member-functions and ensuring they don't get re-introduced?

> and weren't around to help untangle the issues when it was time to upgrade the compiler.

That makes sense I guess.  I wouldn't have thought removing a couple lines from a couple .clang-tidy files would be so time consuming but maybe there is more to it.

> As a project we made a conscious decision that we want to vet clang-tidy adds

I'm not in all the forums that you are but based on review feedback I've seen and discussions I've had with others, I would not come to this conclusion.

Hi Brad, apologies for the late response.

I agree that having these checks in place is valuable, and I’d definitely like to see them in pldm as well, especially for catching issues early in CI. At the same time, in past clang upgrade cycles, we’ve occasionally seen situations where checks were broken for some time and fixes took a while, largely due to limited maintainer bandwidth. In such cases, it has often required additional effort from other maintainers (including Patrick) to get things back into a good state.There have also been prior community discussions (e.g., on Discord) reflecting these experiences. My understanding is that the current approach of keeping a common set of clang-tidy checks was a practical outcome of those discussions, aiming to balance code quality with maintainability across the project. I’m trying to stay aligned with that direction. If the proposed checks are reasonable and we have enough support, I don’t expect it would take too long to move forward. I’d just suggest giving the discussion a bit more time so we can reach alignment as a community.

> Hi Brad, apologies for the late response.

It's no problem.

I certainly don't want to pressure maintainers into merging clang-tidy checks that they think will break or be a hassle to maintain.  I could be wrong, but I doubt the cpp core guidelines checks have caused any such problems.  I just wonder if some nuanced consideration is warranted, so progress can be made in parallel with other alignment discussions...because I don't share your optimism on alignment being reached anytime soon.
Removed the configuration from .clang-tidy and left the fixes.
